author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In the heart of war-ravaged Mosul, two carved lions stand as a fragile link to the city’s shattered past. Bashar, a fisherman, lost his once-grand family home during the battle to liberate the city from ISIL (ISIS) nearly 10 years ago. All that remains is a marble gate crowned with lions, which he fiercely guards.

Fakhri, a devoted collector determined to save Mosul’s heritage, becomes obsessed with acquiring the lions gate for his unofficial museum. His friend Fadil, a musician once silenced under ISIL, challenges him to see the human cost behind every artefact. As Mosul rebuilds, a quiet cultural revival reflects the resilience of a city with 8,000 years of history.

The Lions by the River Tigris is a documentary film by Zaradasht Ahmed.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Paraguay has sworn in a new president after Santiago Pena was impeached and placed under house arrest. Celebrations followed outside Congress.

The Senate voted to impeach Pena for failing to carry out his presidential responsibilities, after the Prosecutor for Economic and Corruption Crimes ordered that he be put under house arrest. Pena is allegedly embroiled in a financial scandal that led to the collapse of the country’s largest online bank, Ueno Bank, this week, leaving millions of depositors unable to access their savings.

Also arrested was Carlos Carvallo, Central Bank president until he was forced to resign. He allegedly covered up serious financial irregularities at Ueno Bank, among other accusations.

His replacement, former vice president Pedro Alliana, was sworn in quickly. He vowed to govern for the most disadvantaged and said citizens affected by the financial crisis “will be fully compensated”. Millions fear losing their savings.

Al Jazeera’s Lucia Newman reports.

Su
title: Paraguay swears in Pedro Alliana after Santiago Pena impeachment

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Activists have entered a construction site in Amsterdam where Microsoft is building a data centre of three towers, each 86 metres high. It is said to use as much electricity as most Amsterdam households, one reason for the anger. Police forbade journalists from going inside.

Activist Sam van der Beek says Amsterdam has enough data centres and Microsoft is “taking our land and resources” to invest its money.

At a Global Switch data centre, servers store everything from medical records to cat videos. Al Jazeera’s reporter says data storage and artificial intelligence use more power than the Netherlands can provide because the grid is overloaded.

Stijn Grove of the Dutch Data Centre Association says there is a good debate, but the industry decided to join the race and must find the best way to do it.

Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen reports from Amsterdam.
